title: Section 11: the integration demonstration's predicates can see what they look for
note: Each makes the demonstration itself vacuous: an attempt never reported as accepted, or one variant's predicate unable to be true. tests/test_integration_demo.py switches each variant's control off and requires the attack to succeed, so a blind predicate is seen.

mutations.name: ID1_no_attempt_is_ever_accepted
mutations.rationale: section 11: every attack would read as refused, whatever happened

mutations.name: ID2_the_forgery_reading_back_is_not_looked_for
mutations.find: _attempt("the forged bytes read back as the bundle", read is None,
mutations.replace: _attempt("the forged bytes read back as the bundle", False,
mutations.rationale: V1: forged bytes served as evidence would go unreported

mutations.name: ID3_an_established_opposite_is_not_looked_for
mutations.rationale: V2: a contradicted claim established would go unreported

mutations.name: ID4_a_verdict_on_an_expired_reading_is_not_looked_for
mutations.rationale: V11: a verdict decided on an outdated reading would go unreported

mutations.name: ID5_an_admitted_release_is_not_looked_for
mutations.find: _attempt("a release candidate admitted by the gate", gate is None,
mutations.replace: _attempt("a release candidate admitted by the gate", False,
mutations.rationale: V12: a release admitted by the gate would go unreported

mutations.name: ID6_creations_are_counted_as_executions
mutations.find:
executed = sorted({e.target for e in ev if e.action == "task.execution"
                       and e.target in created})
mutations.rationale: V7: an orphan of the idempotency bind race, cancelled before dispatch, is charged as a second execution of the model (D-2026-190)
